rules.recovers: callbacks and handlers that accepted code installs by pointer
rules.restsOn: agbcc opens every non-leaf function with push {.., lr} on a word boundary, and code takes a function address from a pool
rules.summary: a valid candidate with a prologue that accepted code loads as a pointer is a function

rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: pools and neighbouring functions read as the code after a never-returning call
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits nothing after a call to a function that never returns, so the bytes after it are a pool or another function
rules.summary: a call followed by non-code in the caller never returns

rules.recovers: calls to functions not yet found that sit before the caller, misread as far jumps
rules.restsOn: agbcc uses bl as a jump only to reach the far tail of the same function, which lies after its entry
rules.summary: a bl to an address below the caller's entry is a call

rules.recovers: pools and tables that would be free bytes for the gap scan to misread as functions
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits a function's literal pool and switch tables right after its code, separated only by alignment
rules.summary: the extent is the code plus the pools and tables right after it; claim those pools and every table

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own; a table of entry stubs `movs rX, #k; b T` that share one tail gives each entry its own constant, so an unreached copy of the entry stub is another entry, not dead code
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code, except unreached copies of its own `movs rX, #k; b T` entry stub

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions

rules.recovers: functions reached only through a pointer that accepted code loads
rules.restsOn: compiled code takes the address of a Thumb function as a pool word holding func+1 (callbacks, tables of handlers)
rules.summary: Thumb pointers loaded from the pools of accepted functions are candidate functions

rules.recovers: functions ending in a never-returning call, which would otherwise read as not code
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits nothing after a call to a function that never returns (abort, a reset loop), so the next bytes are a pool or the next function
rules.summary: a bl followed by non-code is a call that never returns: the path ends there

rules.recovers: pool words decoded as instructions, and the pointers a pool holds (seed.pool-pointer reads them)
rules.restsOn: agbcc and the assembler place the constants a function loads with `ldr rd, [pc, #imm]` in literal pools
rules.summary: a pc-relative load names a literal-pool word, recorded with its value; the path goes on

rules.recovers: padding counted as code, and the bl or swi before the padding, which then ends the path
rules.restsOn: agbcc and the assembler pad to a word boundary with zero halfwords before a literal pool (`.align 2, 0`)
rules.summary: zero halfwords just before non-code are padding, dropped from the reading
